card.name: Digits inside numbers and references
card.fires_on: A single digit (mostly 0, sometimes 5 or 2) placed inside or at the start of a number. Typical settings are a zero count before a slash in trial results, a DOI or date, and page counts.

modes.label: Zero count in trial rates
modes.description: The digit 0 as the numerator of a count such as 0/934 in adverse reaction tables.
modes.example: these atomoxetine hydrochloride patients compared with 0% (<<0>>/934) of placebo patients

modes.label: Digit in DOI or citation
modes.description: A digit following an initial 1 in a reference code or number.

modes.label: Digit in dates and page counts
modes.description: A digit inside a date, rating count or page count on web pages.

card.writes: It promotes unit words like minutes and Chinese time or age units, and suppresses other digits, so it points toward a number ending and a unit.
card.plain: It fires on a digit within a number, often a zero in a count like 0/500, and nudges the text toward a unit rather than more digits.
